Triggers.value: A memory of the event coming to mind suddenly

Threat.value: I feel threatened by strangers approaching me even in ordinary situations
I find it harder to feel safe at night than during the day

Memory.value: Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning
When I remember the event I feel intense rage
Sometimes I feel the full emotional intensity of the event without any clear image or memory

Negative Appraisals.value: My body keeps reacting as if I am still in danger even when I am safe
I will never forgive myself for not doing more to stop what happened

vignette: Ajay, a 29-year-old South Asian man and shopowner in his community, has been struggling with the aftermath of physical abuse by his romantic partner. The trauma has left him feeling constantly on guard, particularly when he encounters certain triggers that remind him of the incident. Ajay’s primary trigger is the scent of sweat or body odour, which transports him back to the night of the attack. He recalls the overpowering smell as his partner approached, and this olfactory cue continues to evoke a sense of immediate danger whenever it surfaces in his environment. Ajay finds himself becoming increasingly vigilant at night, when he feels particularly unsafe and on edge. The darkness seems to amplify every sound, each shadowy figure outside his shop evoking the memory of that night. His nights are plagued with trouble falling or staying asleep, as he constantly worries about a repeat attack. Even certain conversation topics, such as relationships or physical intimacy, can suddenly trigger intense memories, causing him to feel on high alert and overwhelmed by the threat of danger. When these triggers occur, Ajay is instantly transported back to the event, feeling the rage that accompanies the memory. The emotional intensity often surges without a clear image, leaving him with a visceral sense of dread. He has come to believe his body is betraying him, reacting as if he were still in immediate danger even when he’s safe. Ajay struggles deeply with feelings of guilt for not stopping what happened, which compounds his anxiety and further undermines his confidence in himself. Ajay's negative appraisals have become a self-reinforcing cycle that has significantly affected his life. He believes he can’t rely on himself to protect himself or make sound decisions when faced with threats, leading him to avoid situations that might trigger these memories or fears. This avoidance has extended into his daily routine; he often closes the shop early and avoids social gatherings where he might encounter strong smells or certain conversation topics. His partner’s presence in his life continues to be a source of profound distress. Ajay finds it increasingly difficult to trust her, even though she no longer abuses him. He remains hypervigilant, always on edge, and this constant state of alertness has taken a toll on their relationship. The memory of the event often comes unbidden during everyday moments, like walking past someone who smells similar or overhearing a conversation that touches on sensitive topics. Ajay’s negative appraisals have led him to feel increasingly isolated, as if he can’t trust his own judgment in assessing threats. This internal struggle has created a feedback loop where the memory of the event triggers heightened threat perceptions, which then reinforce his sense of helplessness and inability to rely on himself. He is certain that this cycle will only continue unless he finds a way to break it. The cumulative impact of these symptoms has left Ajay feeling trapped in a cycle of fear and avoidance. The constant vigilance and emotional turmoil have begun to affect his ability to manage the shop effectively, as well as his relationship with his partner. What finally brought him to seek help was an overwhelming sense that he could no longer cope alone and a deep hope for relief from these debilitating symptoms. Ajay is most afraid of feeling powerless and vulnerable again, reliving the trauma in every trigger. He hopes for a return to a life where he feels safe and can trust himself and his environment once more.
